body:
## Problem

If the compiled GUI runtime completes an admitted action and verifies input release, then a `verify_effect` callback exception escapes without a typed receipt. A journal callback can also fail after the action has completed. Catching these exceptions at the shared runtime boundary must preserve the completed prefix without defeating adapter-owned evidence retention.

## Change

Convert verifier callback exceptions to `RUNTIME_FAILED/effect_unavailable` receipts and journal callback exceptions to `RUNTIME_FAILED/execution_failed`. Preserve the completed transition, verified release, pending effect and in-memory critical failure evidence, then stop without another observation/action or success claim. The Guarded X11 adapter first retains its `effect_verification` exception witness, then re-raises to the shared graph. A failed journal sink is not retried or described as durable evidence.

## Validation

- Current-main reproductions for verifier and journal exceptions; typed candidate regressions cover both.
- Guarded X11 fake-Bridge suite: 30/30 PASS, including retained raw exception witness and typed receipt.
- `runtime/core_v1` suite: 96/96 PASS; byte-compilation and `git diff --check` pass.
- Python 3.12.14; `python-xlib==0.33` installed only to an isolated output target for an existing lazy import.
- No display, GUI, app, game, model/provider, container or formal allocation was used.
- Latest pushed head: `f18c378f1eef3f48ea10207e17eb7f184bb5d8a5`, base `402c7d1b5147b2a905098f082233db60a47d68db`; hosted checks pending at push.

Other adapter exceptions and recovery after a failed journal sink remain outside scope. This does not complete #57's integrated live-efficiency milestone.

comments.body:
## Reply to technical review: adapter exception witness loss

Confirmed against the reviewed head: `compiled_gui.run()` returned the intended `RUNTIME_FAILED/effect_unavailable` receipt after one fake input, but the Guarded X11 bridge saved zero `*-exception.json` records. The adapter now catches the verifier exception only to retain a scoped `effect_verification` witness (`error_type`, `repr`, `replay_allowed:false`, effect status unknown), then re-raises it for the shared graph's typed fail-closed receipt. The new fake-Bridge regression asserts one completed action, retained pending effect, one input only, exactly one saved exception witness and a saved receipt. The Guarded X11 compile doc now describes this behavior.

Verification after the repair: Guarded X11 fake-Bridge test suite 30/30 PASS with `python-xlib==0.33` installed only under an isolated output target; `runtime/core_v1` 96/96 PASS; byte-compilation and `git diff --check` PASS. No display, model, app, game, or physical input was used. Formal allocation remains uninvoked. Other adapter exceptions and raw-witness persistence failures remain outside this repair.

Self-check finding on the exact current-main + PR head merge tree (`03d3884037d279fd4a078aee479c6fb1e6757434`): the journal-failure handling misses a terminal journal exception when the run is already `RUNTIME_FAILED` for another reason.

Reproduction used only local fake callbacks: `verify_effect` raises `RuntimeError`, then the journal callback raises `OSError` on `runtime_finished`. The returned receipt remains `RUNTIME_FAILED/effect_unavailable`, and `critical_events` has the verifier failure and `runtime_finished` but no `journal_write_failed`. Since `emit()` appends `runtime_finished` before attempting the journal callback, the final `finish()` condition `journal_failure_type is not None and outcome != "RUNTIME_FAILED"` skips recording the second failure. This hides that the terminal receipt itself could not be journaled.

This is a self-check observation, not an independent review or approval.

title: fix(#57): preserve compiled receipts on callback failure
